_comment: 🎨️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform: `quick-xml` 0.42 registered as the independent reference reader/writer for SVG 1.1 `any` mutation coverage, the exhaustive 11-kind `SvgMutation` vocabulary it is measured against, and the tolerant-numeric comparison profile the decomposed `viewBox`/`transform` geometry needs. The shared stdio manifest does not register `quick-xml` under any `svg-*` capability at all (only the 📰xml 1.0 subset, a sibling owner, reaches it for its own vocabulary), so this is a first registration, not a reuse.

oracles.rationale: quick-xml is a general streaming XML reader AND writer (not SVG-specific), used here as the independent parser/serializer against which this subset's own hand-rolled `xml_document_from_text`/`xml_document_to_text` codec is measured. This subset's oracle module (../🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs) builds its own small in-memory element tree from quick-xml's event stream, applies each declared `SvgMutation` kind to that tree using independently hand-written viewBox/transform grammars (never importing this subset's production parsers), and re-serializes with quick-xml's `Writer`. The projection sorts attributes by name (SVG attribute order is writer freedom, never normative) and decomposes the `viewBox`/`transform` attribute STRINGS into typed numeric geometry rather than comparing their raw text, since two independently-written formatters are not guaranteed to produce byte-identical number formatting even when the underlying value is identical -- everything else (attribute names/values, element names, text/CDATA/comment/PI content, namespace-declaration attributes, xlink:href) is compared as exact raw strings.

comparisonProfiles.description: SVG 1.1 mutation round trips compared structurally: element/text/CDATA/comment/PI tree shape and content exact, attributes compared as a name-sorted set (SVG attribute order is real writer freedom -- see this subset's own `write_svg_xml`, which never claims to preserve source attribute order beyond update-in-place), and the `viewBox`/`transform` attribute values specifically decomposed into typed numeric geometry (never compared as raw strings) with a small absolute tolerance for cross-implementation float-formatting noise between quick-xml's writer and this subset's own. Self-closing vs explicit empty open/close tags are equivalent by construction (both parse to zero children) and never distinguished by either side.
